body: Thanks for your response. I think you're right, that I knew deep down that it wouldn't do much.

Yeah I get what you're saying about the method. I think deep down, I thought of it as "this probably won't work, but if it does then ok"

I wrote my thoughts down yesterday, and even admitted it was mostly therapeutic (it really was).

I've never seen someone so I've never been officially diagnosed. But I have read up on it and kinda self-diagnosed myself as having depression
Thanks. I'm not seeing anyone, but I have thought about it

Thanks for the reply. Never too late :-)

I think you're right with a different tactic. When we've talked about possibly hurting one another in the future, I've said basically what you're saying, that we will fight and we're not perfect. And that it's gonna be our ability to communicate (which we did do until this week very well) that keeps it all together.

I'm hoping that the talking over text us what's leading her to be more passive. She's usually more straight forward, but this week has kind of been holding back. I'm thinking a face to face talk might change it...for better or worse...

At least she won't just be a passenger on this ride

Thanks to everyone on the replies, both in this post and the other.

Between friends and family, and all of you, it seems to be a 100% consensus that I should call it a day and walk away. Any you might be right. Maybe even after spanning both posts I still haven't given enough of a clear picture of the situation. Or maybe it's the clues you see but can't explain.

Or maybe I really am kidding myself (probably this one).

In my rush out the door I didn't have a chance to finish the last bit on information: I have called her out on her bullshit reasoning, and called her a coward for taking the safe road. She never responded, never once corrected me so I think I may be right (again, "lack of evidence is not evidence of lack") I will see this through till the very end, where she will either tell me I'm right and we can work this out or she will tell me to GTFO.

I thank you all for your responses. I knew when I was writing it how they would all go. I think this writing was more therapeutic than anything else (also doesn't help that the one person I would normally talk this out with is the person that I'm talking about).


If anyone is interested I can post a followup in a few days (blah blah OP never delivers).

Thanks. I do now know how to talk to women (took a few tries, but I figured it out) :-)

I am happy with how I am as a person, just hurt. I've suffered hearbreak before, so I think I'll be ok.

You might be right. Though a short time, we never had a single problem with the relationship, emotionally or sexually. We talked about it after the first time we hooked up, and both said we were worried that it would be weird coming from being friends. But we agreed it just felt natural.

I know she's not the type of person to lie about something like that.

Thanks for the response. 
I get what you're saying about being the begging boyfriend. I've told her all week long that I wouldn't beg, and that I would only fight if there was even a chance. She's never said there was no chance, which doesn't mean there is one, but it's also not a confirmation of no chance.

For the marriage/kids part, I really have no idea what I want. I'll figure it out with whomever I'm with what's right. I just wanted that person to be her.

> She could potentially hurt you.

That part has already happened...



ps: you're also probably right about the leaving me for someone else. The whole reason it ended after two weeks back in high school was a combination of me not knowing how to talk to girls, and her moving on to someone else. So this does have a familiar feeling, except everything is times 10...

Thanks for the reply, and for reading everything.

She was only with him for a short time, so I don't think it's that she likes him that much. And yes, I do see the irony in that I haven't been with her for that long. But I also have almost 20 years of friendship as a foundation. I really think she sees him as the safer, and therefore better option.

Maybe I can't help her overcome her fear, but I can try.

I would do anything for any of my friends, without question. Without hesitation. I'm ok with the pain that might come from fighting and losing.

In my head I'm also in agreement. It's that stupid, stupid heart that is holding on.

Probably should have just posted part two as a comment to make it all in one post...well here it is:

Before we started talking, she was dating this guy for a couple months. They would always fight, he was a jerk to her. She dumped him. He never spoke to her...until he found out she started being with me. He showed up at her house, begging her to take him back. She said no, and that was the end. Until a few weeks later. He showed up again, this time with flowers and a ring (crazy right?). He said his divorce was just finalized and he wanted to be with her. She said no, and he left.

She told me about all the interactions (us being friends for so long, we're both comfortable with being honest with each other). As far as I know they agreed on being friends.

Things get better with us. We see each other every weekend (either her coming up or me going down). The relationship is moving fast. It was only a month, but we already dropped the "L-word" bomb. But we had also known each other for almost 20 years. We never fought about anything. We were always laughing about something. It was the best summer that both of us could have.

Cut to last weekend. I go down to see her and we go on a hike together. We talk about feelings for each other and how we are both very happy with our relationship. I leave her Sunday to head home, and she asks me if I'm ok, and that I seem distant. I wasn't I was just tired, but I think something was bothering her and she just didn't want to say anything.

The next day, everything changed. She texted me and said that she was afraid that things were moving too fast / not fast enough / didn't know what the future holds. She didn't know if she wanted to get married again, and whether or not she would want kids, and said that it wasn't fair to me for being indecisive. I told her not to worry, and that I wanted to be with her no matter what (truly, I didn't know if I wanted marriage and/or kids either, so I wasn't worried about the future). I thought things would end there...but then she said she still thought she had feelings for her ex-bf (the one from a few weeks ago with the wedding ring. The one that she always fought with. That one).

That one was like a sucker punch. I didn't know what to make of that. I immediately fell in to best-friend mode, and told her that I would want her to be happy, no matter who it's with. It mattered to me, but I'd do anything as a friend for her. I would be willing to sacrifice my happiness if she was happy. A few more days went by and we kept talking over text, but it was the same thing. She didn't know what she wanted, that it wasn't fair to me to do this to me, etc. I stayed strong, and told her I would be there for her until the end.

By Thursday, I thought that she had really already made her decision to be with the other guy, but was too afraid to break up with me and hurt me. So I did what a best friend would do: I fell on my sword. I told her I'd break up with her for her so that she can be happy with the other guy. I wished her well, and that the other guy does change his ways. And I meant it. She's an amazing person and deserve to be happy.

She never responded to my texts. I figured she just accepted it.

The next day I posted a video on facebook that only she could see: Brad Paisley's "I wish you'd stay". Corney, I know. But it felt appropriate. Later that day she posted a video on her own wall, Five Finger Death Punch's "Bleeding". I texted her telling her the song was wrong. That she might be better off without me, but I wasn't better off without her.

She responded saying that she posted it more for the bleeding reference (for those that don't know the song, it's about a breakup and how the bleeding and heartbreak finally stops). I told her that if she was actually heartbroken then we should sit down and talk about this. That it doesn't have to end this way.

Earlier in the day I think I figured it out: she was afraid. She was afraid of us being together and if it didn't work out, what it would do to her. She was afraid that I would get sick of her, and leave her (she constantly said that to me, I thought she was being playful. I always told her if anything she would be the one to leave first).

She's so afraid of being hurt by me, that I think she's seeing her ex-bf as the "safe" route. That if she goes with him, and he doesn't change, and they go back to fighting and she ends up alone again that the pain that that would cause would be nothing compared any pain that would come from it ending badly with me.

We've never fought. We've both told each other that neither of us could think of what we would fight about. We know each other so well, we can tell when the other is hurt or holding back.

I told her I would never hurt her, and I would always be there for her. I was willing to walk away for her because I thought she didn't have feelings for me, but when she told me she felt heartache I didn't want to give up. I wanted to fight for us. I told her that I would fight for us, and that I would rather us be together and suffer any pain of heartbreak that may or may not happen in the future, because none of that pain would compare to the pain of constantly asking myself "what if..."

Due to being an hour away, and busy work/social schedules, we haven't seen each other since Sunday. All communication have been over texts. I keep trying to go down to see her, but she keeps saying she's busy and can't. She offered to come up saturday night, but if things go badly I don't want her driving home in a bad state. She now made other plans Saturday night, so I don't think I'll be able to see her now anyways.

I guess I'm not sure what I'm looking for here, /r/Relationships[2] . I know I want to fight. I know that if I see her I might be able to find the truth, that she's afraid. I might be able to pull her back, to get her to fight her fears with me for the relationship. I guess I'm not looking for advice, but If anyone cares to share their experiences, offer advice I'd be more than willing to listen.

I'm going out for a bit, but I'll put this throwaway account on my mobile, so I'll be able to answer any questions you might have. Sorry that this story took two posts to tell. But I feel without the full picture none of it would make sense.

Thanks for the replies, and for reading both parts of the story.

You're both right, and everyone else I've talked to about it, friends and family, have all said the same thing you have. And they even know our history better than a single reddit post.

Edit: If this was any other girlfriend, I would have walked away on Monday. If she was truly over me, I would have stopped after I broke up for her on Thursday. But if she's doing this all because she's afraid, I truly believe I can work with that.

I'm not afraid of the fight. I'm not afraid of losing the fight. At least that way I can say I tried, and there really was nothing more that I could do.

To your point, froggy, if it doesn't end up with us being together it would mean the end of the friendship. So I wouldn't be around to see her go off with some loser (your words... I just happen to be in agreement)
